sections.title: Disclosure
sections.body: Moontera LLC may obtain motor vehicle records (MVR) about me for employment or driver qualification purposes. These records may include my driving history and CDL information.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body:
By signing below, I authorize Moontera LLC and its authorized service providers, including MVRcheck.com, to obtain and review my motor vehicle records for employment and driver qualification purposes, as permitted by law.

I understand that this authorization may apply during the application process and, if I am hired or contracted, during my service relationship with Moontera LLC to the extent permitted by applicable law.

sections.title: IMPORTANT DISCLOSURE
sections.body:
REGARDING BACKGROUND REPORTS FROM THE PSP Online Service

In connection with your application for employment with Moontera LLC (“Prospective Employer”), Prospective 
Employer, its employees, agents or contractors may obtain one or more reports regarding your driving, and safety inspection history 
from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA). 
When the application for employment is submitted in person, if the Prospective Employer uses any information it obtains from FMCSA 
in a decision to not hire you or to make any other adverse employment decision regarding you, the Prospective Employer will provide 
you with a copy of the report upon which its decision was based and a written summary of your rights under the Fair Credit Reporting 
Act before taking any final adverse action. If any final adverse action is taken against you based upon your driving history or safety 
report, the Prospective Employer will notify you that the action has been taken and that the action was based in part or in whole on this 
report. 
 
When the application for employment is submitted by mail, telephone, computer, or other similar means, if the Prospective Employer 
uses any information it obtains from FMCSA in a decision to not hire you or to make any other adverse employment decision regarding 
you, the Prospective Employer must provide you within three business days of taking adverse action oral, written or electronic 
notification: that adverse action has been taken based in whole or in part on information obtained from FMCSA; the name, address, and 
the toll free telephone number of FMCSA; that the FMCSA did not make the decision to take the adverse action and is unable to provide 
you the specific reasons why the adverse action was taken; and that you may, upon providing proper identification, request a free copy 
of the report and may dispute with the FMCSA the accuracy or completeness of any information or report. If you request a copy of a 
driver record from the Prospective Employer who procured  the report, then, within 3 business days of receiving your request, together 
with proper identification, the Prospective Employer must send or provide to you a copy of your report and a summary of your rights 
under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. 
 
Neither the Prospective Employer nor the FMCSA contractor supplying the crash and safety information has the capability to correct 
any safety data that appears to be incorrect. You may challenge the accuracy of the data by submitting a request to 
https://dataqs.fmcsa.dot.gov. If you challenge crash or inspection information reported by a State, FMCSA cannot change or correct this 
data. Your request will be forwarded by the DataQs system to the appropriate State for adjudication.  
 
Any crash or inspection in which you were involved will display on your PSP report. Since the PSP report does not report, or assign, or 
imply fault, it will include all Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) crashes where you were a driver or co-driver and where those crashes 
were reported to FMCSA, regardless of fault. Similarly, all inspections, with or without violations, appear on the PSP report . State 
citations associated with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSR) violations that have been adjudicated by a court of law 
will also appear, and remain, on a PSP report. 
 
The Prospective Employer cannot obtain background reports from FMCSA without your authorization.

sections.title: Authorization
sections.body:
If you agree that the Prospective Employer may obtain such background reports, please read the following and sign below: 
 
I authorize Moontera LLC (“Prospective Employer”) to access the FMCSA Pre-Employment Screening Program (PSP) 
system to seek information regarding my commercial driving safety record and information regarding my safety inspection history. I 
understand that I am authorizing the release of safety performance information including crash data from the previous five (5) years 
and inspection history from the previous three (3) years. I understand and acknowledge that this release of information may assist the 
Prospective Employer to make a determination regarding my suitability as an employee.  
 
I further understand that neither the Prospective Employer nor the FMCSA contractor supplying the crash and safety information has 
the capability to correct any safety data that appears to be incorrect. I understand I may challenge the accuracy of the data by 
submitting a request to https://dataqs.fmcsa.dot.gov. If I challenge crash or inspection information reported by a State, FMCSA cannot 
change or correct this data. I understand my request will be forwarded by the DataQs system to the appropriate State for adjudication. 
 
I understand that any crash or inspection in which I was involved will display on my PSP report. Since the PSP report does not report, 
or assign, or imply fault, I acknowledge it will include all CMV crashes where I was a driver or co-driver and where those crashes 
were reported to FMCSA, regardless of fault. Similarly, I understand all inspections, with or  without violations, will appear on my 
PSP report, and State citations associated with FMCSR violations that have been adjudicated by a court of law will also appear, and 
remain, on my PSP report.
I have read the above Disclosure Regarding Background Reports provided to me by Prospective Employer and I understand that if I 
sign this Disclosure and Authorization, Prospective Employer may obtain a report of my crash and inspection history. I hereby 
authorize Prospective Employer and its employees, authorized agents, and/or affiliates to obtain the information authorized above. 
 
NOTICE: This form is made available to monthly account holders by NIC on behalf of the U.S. Department of Transportation, 
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA). Account holders are required by federal law to obtain an Applicant’s written 
or electronic consent prior to accessing the Applicant’s PSP report. Further, account holders are required by FMCSA to use the language 
contained in this Disclosure and Authorization form to obtain an Applicant’s consent. The language must be used in whole, exactly as 
provided. Further, the language on this form must exist as one stand-alone document. The language may NOT be included with other 
consent forms or any other language. 
NOTICE: The prospective employment concept referenced in this form contemplates the definition of “employee” contained at 49 
C.F.R. 383.5.
LAST UPDATED 2/11/2016

sections.title: Company notice
sections.body:
This handbook contains company operational policies, safety procedures, FMCSA compliance 
requirements, dispatch procedures, and driver responsibilities applicable to all drivers operating under 
Moontera LLC authority. All drivers are required to review, understand, and comply with the policies 
contained in this handbook as a condition of operating company equipment or operating under 
company authority. Failure to comply with company policies, safety procedures, dispatch instructions, 
or FMCSA regulations may result in disciplinary action, operational penalties, suspension, removal 
from dispatch, contract termination, or termination of employment.
This handbook is intended for internal company use only and may be updated or revised by Moontera 
LLC at any time.

sections.title: 1. DRIVER ACKNOWLEDGMENT
sections.body:
I acknowledge that I have received the Moontera LLC Driver Safety & Compliance Handbook. I 
understand that I am required to comply with all company rules, operational procedures, FMCSA 
regulations, dispatch instructions, and safety requirements while operating under company authority.
I understand that failure to comply with company policies may result in disciplinary action, 
suspension, operational penalties, removal from dispatch, contract termination, or termination of 
employment.

sections.title: 2. COMPANY SAFETY POLICY
sections.body:
Moontera LLC is committed to maintaining a safe, professional, and compliant transportation 
operation. Safety is the responsibility of every driver operating under company authority.
Drivers are expected to:
-operate safely and professionally at all times,
-comply with FMCSA regulations,
-protect company equipment and customer freight,
-maintain proper communication with dispatch,
-avoid unsafe or reckless operation,
-report accidents, damages, and safety concerns immediately.
Unsafe driving, negligence, policy violations, cargo mishandling, log falsi fication, or conduct 
negatively affecting company safety scores may result in disciplinary action up to and including 
termination.

sections.title: 3. SEATBELT POLICY
sections.body:
All drivers and passengers operating or riding in company equipment must wear seatbelts at all times 
while the vehicle is in motion.
Failure to wear a seatbelt violates company policy and FMCSA safety expectations.
Repeated violations may result in:
-safety disciplinary action,
-suspension from dispatch,
-operational penalties,
-or termination.
Drivers are responsible for ensuring compliance by any passenger riding in company equipment.

sections.title: 4. CELL PHONE & DISTRACTED DRIVING POLICY
sections.body:
Moontera LLC strictly prohibits distracted driving.
Drivers are prohibited from:
-texting while driving,
-reading messages while operating a vehicle,
-manually entering GPS information while driving,
-using handheld mobile devices,
-watching videos or social media while operating equipment.
Hands-free devices may be used only when operation can be performed safely and in compliance 
with FMCSA regulations.
If emergency communication is necessary, the driver must safely park the vehicle before using a 
handheld device.
Violations may result in:
-operational penalties,
-suspension,
-loss of dispatch priority,
-FMCSA citations,
-or termination.
Drivers are personally responsible for citations, fines, or penalties issued by enforcement agencies for 
distracted driving violations.

sections.title: 5. HOURS OF SERVICE (HOS) POLICY
sections.body:
Drivers must comply with all FMCSA Hours of Service regulations.
Drivers may not:
-exceed 11 driving hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty,
-drive after the 14-hour duty window expires,
-violate 60/70-hour limits,
-falsify logs,
-operate while fatigued,
-hide violations or manipulate ELD records.
Drivers are responsible for:
-monitoring available hours,
-proper ELD usage,
-maintaining supporting documentation,
-immediately reporting ELD malfunctions.
Repeated violations, falsification, or unsafe operation related to fatigue may result in:
-retraining,
-suspension,
-operational penalties,
-removal from dispatch,
-or termination.
Moontera LLC reserves the right to review:
-fuel receipts,
-toll records,
-GPS tracking,
-dispatch records,
-and customer timestamps
to verify HOS compliance.

sections.title: 6. DASHCAM & RECORDING POLICY
sections.body:
Company equipment may contain:
-inward-facing cameras,
-outward-facing cameras,
-GPS tracking systems,
-telematics systems,
-audio/video monitoring systems.
These systems may be used for:
-safety monitoring,
-accident investigation,
-cargo claim review,
-FMCSA compliance,
-operational review,
-insurance defense,
-driver coaching.
Drivers operating under company authority consent to monitoring and recording while operating 
company equipment.
Tampering with, disconnecting, obstructing, or damaging camera systems or tracking equipment is 
strictly prohibited.
Violations may result in:
-immediate suspension,
-chargebacks for damaged equipment,
-or termination.

sections.title: 7. DRUG & ALCOHOL POLICY
sections.body:
Moontera LLC complies with all FMCSA drug and alcohol testing regulations.
Drivers are prohibited from:
-operating under the influence of alcohol,
-operating under illegal substances,
-using prohibited controlled substances,
-refusing required testing.
Drivers may be subject to:
-pre-employment testing,
-random testing,
-post-accident testing,
-reasonable suspicion testing.
Refusal to submit to required testing will be treated as a policy violation.
Drivers must immediately disclose any medication that may affect safe operation.
Violations may result in:
-immediate removal from duty,
-termination,
-FMCSA reporting,
-and legal consequences.

sections.title: 8. PRE-TRIP / POST-TRIP INSPECTION POLICY
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for performing proper inspections before and after operating company 
equipment.
Inspections must include:
-tires,
-brakes,
-lights,
-air systems,
-fluids,
-securement equipment,
-trailer condition,
-safety equipment,
-load securement.
Drivers must immediately report:
-defects,
-warning lights,
-maintenance concerns,
-tire damage,
-trailer damage,
-unsafe operating conditions.
Operating unsafe equipment may result in disciplinary action.
Failure to report equipment issues causing additional damages may result in operational penalties or 
chargebacks.

sections.title: 9. PPE & SAFETY EQUIPMENT POLICY
sections.body:
Drivers must maintain required safety equipment in company vehicles.
Required equipment may include:
-reflective vest,
-gloves,
-flashlight,
-warning triangles,
-fire extinguisher,
-load securement equipment,
-safety straps and locks.
Drivers must follow customer and facility PPE requirements at all times.
Failure to maintain or use required safety equipment may result in:
-disciplinary action,
-removal from facilities,
-cargo delays,
-operational penalties.

sections.title: 10. NON-SMOKING & TRUCK CLEANLINESS POLICY
sections.body:
Smoking is prohibited inside company equipment unless specifically authorized.
Drivers are responsible for maintaining:
-clean truck interiors,
-organized sleeper areas,
-professional vehicle appearance,
-proper disposal of trash,
-sanitary conditions.
Drivers may be held responsible for:
-excessive cleaning expenses,
-interior damages,
-smoke-related damages,
-neglect-related conditions.
Repeated violations may result in:
-operational penalties,
-cleaning chargebacks,
-suspension,

sections.title: 11. DISPATCH COMMUNICATION POLICY
sections.body:
Drivers must maintain active communication with dispatch at all times while operating under company 
authority.
Drivers are responsible for immediately reporting:
-delays,
-detention,
-breakdowns,
-accidents,
-roadside inspections,
-customer issues,
-load problems,
-appointment issues.
Failure to communicate properly may negatively affect:
-customer relationships,
-broker ratings,
-safety scores,
-dispatch operations.
Repeated communication failures, unauthorized delays, missed appointments, or ignoring dispatch 
instructions may result in:
-reduction of dispatch priority,
-operational penalties,
-suspension,
-or termination.

sections.title: 12. DRIVER RESPONSIBILITIES & CONDUCT
sections.body:
Drivers are expected to conduct themselves professionally at all times.
Drivers are responsible for:
-protecting company equipment,
-protecting customer freight,
-maintaining professionalism,
-following dispatch instructions,
-complying with FMCSA regulations,
-maintaining accurate documentation,
-operating safely and responsibly.
Drivers may not:
-abandon equipment,
-transport unauthorized passengers,
-use company equipment for unauthorized purposes,
-engage in reckless driving,
-intentionally damage company property.
Negligence, unsafe conduct, customer complaints, preventable damages, or policy violations may 
result in disciplinary action up to termination.

sections.title: 13. LOAD & DOCUMENT HANDLING POLICY
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for properly handling customer freight and transportation documents.
Drivers must:
-verify load information before departure,
-check seal condition,
-request “SLC” when applicable,
-request “Seal Intact” notation at delivery,
-verify piece counts when required,
-protect shipping documents,
-submit PODs promptly.
Drivers must immediately report:
-shortages,
-overages,
-damages,
-rejected freight,
-temperature issues,
-seal discrepancies.
Failure to properly secure, monitor, or report cargo conditions may result in:
-cargo claims,
-operational penalties,
-chargebacks,
-or termination.

sections.title: 14. OPERATIONAL PENALTIES & DISCIPLINE POLICY
sections.body:
Moontera LLC maintains strict operational and safety standards.
The company reserves the right to apply disciplinary action, operational penalties, chargebacks, 
suspension, or termination for preventable operational failures including but not limited to:
-late pickups,
-late deliveries,
-unauthorized stops,
-communication failures,
-HOS violations,
-roadside inspection violations,
-cargo securement violations,
-preventable accidents,
-equipment neglect,
-excessive idling,
-abandoned equipment,
-customer complaints,
-damaged freight,
-unsafe operation.
Additional operational review guidelines may include:
-Preventable service failures: subject to operational review
-Cargo claims caused by negligence: subject to claim review
-Excessive truck cleaning or damages: subject to cleaning or repair expenses
Any operational penalties, deductions, or chargebacks will be supported by documentation and 
handled in accordance with applicable laws and contractual agreements.
The company reserves the right to determine appropriate disciplinary action based on:
-severity,
-frequency,
-safety impact,
-customer impact,
-operational damages.

sections.title: 15. CONTRACTOR FINES & PENALTIES
sections.body:
If the Contractor does not keep the Equipment operating for the full Term, the fines, penalties, and/or fees paid to any regulatory agency by the Company to certify such Equipment or drivers may be deducted from Escrow or Payment.

Any other fines, penalties, and/or fees assessed to the Company by the U.S. Department of Transportation or any other regulatory agency as a result of the Contractor's action, inaction, or negligence may be passed on to the Contractor and deducted from Escrow or Payment.

Charges are based on a charge-per-severity-point system: 1 point = $100 for each violation point received. For example, a violation with a total severity of 3 points results in a $300 charge.

This charge-per-severity-point system applies to:
-Unsafe Driving: after the third violation, the contract with the driver will be terminated.
-Hours of Service (HOS): after the third violation, the contract with the driver will be terminated.
-Vehicle Maintenance: after the third violation, the contract with the driver will be terminated.
-Driver Fitness: after the third violation, the contract with the driver will be terminated.
-Controlled Substances and Alcohol: a charge and immediate termination of the contract with the driver.

Additional inspection penalties:
-Failed Level I inspection: $300 charge.
-Failed Level II inspection: $200 charge.
-Failed Level III inspection: $100 charge.

sections.title: 16. DRIVER RECOGNITION & INSPECTION BONUSES
sections.body:
Drivers who consistently submit accurate, true, neat, and legible logs will be recognized for their superior efforts.

Inspection bonuses:
-Level I inspection with no violations: $300 bonus.
-Level II inspection with no violations: $200 bonus.
-Level III inspection with no violations: $100 bonus.

sections.title: 17. CONTRACTOR ESCROW
sections.body:
The Contractor authorizes the Company to withhold $250.00 per week for 10 consecutive weeks, up to a maximum of $2,500.00, to be held in an escrow account maintained by the Company ("Escrow").

All escrow funds may be held for up to 60 days following termination of the Agreement to ensure payment of the Contractor's obligations, including, but not limited to, fuel taxes, cargo claims, liability claims, advances, fuel card advances, or any other costs for which the Contractor is responsible.

If any claims remain unresolved at the end of the 60-day period, the Company may retain the escrow funds until all claims are settled. Any remaining escrow funds will be released within 60 days after the resolution of all outstanding claims.

The Contractor must return all Company-issued license plates before any escrow funds will be released. Failure to return the plates will result in forfeiture of the escrow funds.

The Contractor's final paycheck will be held for three (3) weeks following their departure from the Company.

sections.title: 18. CONTRACTOR TERMINATION & NOTICES
sections.body:
If the Contractor decides to terminate the Agreement, the Contractor must provide the Company with two (2) weeks' notice.

If the Contractor fails to provide such notice, the Company shall be entitled to withhold the driver's last settlement pay as well as any escrow funds collected from the Contractor.

In the event of termination, the Contractor's last settlement pay will be released only upon return of Company property, including, but not limited to, the truck, trailer, ELD device, and Company paperwork.

The truck and/or trailer must be returned to the Company location according to Company instructions. The Contractor is obligated to contact the Company and obtain those instructions.

sections.title: 19. FINAL DRIVER ACKNOWLEDGMENT
sections.body:
I acknowledge that I have received, reviewed, and understood the Moontera LLC Driver Safety & 
Compliance Handbook.
I understand that I am responsible for complying with company policies, FMCSA regulations, dispatch 
instructions, and safety procedures while operating under company authority.
I understand that policy violations may result in disciplinary action, suspension, operational penalties, 
chargebacks, removal from dispatch, contract termination, or termination of employment.

sections.title: Company notice
sections.body:
This document contains required cargo handling procedures, freight protection expectations, 
shipping document requirements, seal control procedures, and claims prevention policies 
applicable to all drivers operating under Moontera LLC authority.
Drivers are responsible for properly handling, protecting, securing, monitoring, and delivering 
customer freight in accordance with company procedures and customer requirements.
Failure to comply with cargo handling procedures may negatively impact customer relationships, 
broker ratings, insurance protection, cargo claims, and company operations.
Failure to follow the procedures contained in this document may result in disciplinary action, 
operational penalties, chargebacks, suspension, removal from dispatch, contract termination, or 
termination of employment.
In addition, all drivers are expected to maintain professional communication with brokers, 
shippers, receivers, dispatch personnel, warehouse staff, and customers at all times while 
operating under Moontera LLC authority. Drivers must immediately report delays, cargo 
discrepancies, detention issues, rejected freight, damaged freight, temperature variances, seal 
issues, accidents, citations, roadside inspections, or any situation that may impact safe and timely 
delivery. Drivers are also responsible for maintaining accurate shipment updates, preserving 
shipping documentation, following all FMCSA safety regulations, and protecting company 
equipment, customer property, and freight from loss, theft, contamination, or unauthorized access 
during transport.

sections.title: 1. FREIGHT HANDLING RESPONSIBILITIES
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for protecting customer freight while operating under company authority.
Drivers must:
-inspect freight condition,
-verify load information,
-monitor cargo during transit,
-protect shipping documents,
-maintain proper communication with dispatch,
-report issues immediately.
Drivers are expected to operate professionally and minimize risks involving:
-cargo damage,
-freight shortages,
-load shifts,
-seal issues,
-rejected freight,
-temperature deviations,
-late deliveries.
Negligence involving freight protection may result in operational penalties, cargo claim liability 
review, suspension, or termination.

sections.title: 2. PICKUP PROCEDURES
sections.body:
Drivers must properly inspect and verify freight during pickup.
Drivers must:
-verify pickup information,
-confirm load number,
-inspect trailer condition,
-inspect cargo packaging,
-verify piece counts when required,
-verify temperature requirements,
-inspect seal condition when applicable.
Drivers should request “SLC” (Shipper Load Counted) notation when applicable.
Drivers must immediately report:
-damaged freight,
-broken packaging,
-overloaded conditions,
-unsafe loading,
-improper temperature,
-missing freight,
-hazmat concerns.
Drivers may not depart pickup locations with unresolved freight concerns without company 
authorization.

sections.title: 3. DELIVERY PROCEDURES
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for properly delivering customer freight and protecting shipping 
documentation.
Drivers must:
-verify delivery location,
-inspect seal condition,
-supervise unloading when possible,
-protect freight from damage during unloading,
-verify unloading information,
-obtain signatures and delivery documentation.
Drivers should request “Seal Intact” notation when applicable.
Drivers must immediately report:
-shortages,
-overages,
-damages,
-rejected freight,
-detention issues,
-unloading disputes.
Drivers may not leave delivery locations during disputes without company authorization.

sections.title: 4. SEAL CONTROL POLICY
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for maintaining proper seal control procedures.
Drivers must:
-verify seal numbers before departure,
-confirm seal matches shipping documents,
-inspect seal integrity during transit,
-immediately report broken or missing seals.
Drivers may not:
-break seals without authorization when prohibited,
-operate with missing seal documentation,
-ignore seal discrepancies.
Seal violations, missing seals, or unreported seal issues may result in:
-cargo claims,
-customer complaints,
-operational penalties,
-disciplinary action.

sections.title: 5. BOL & POD REQUIREMENTS
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for properly handling transportation documents.
Required documents may include:
-Bill of Lading (BOL),
-Proof of Delivery (POD),
-lumper receipts,
-scale tickets,
-temperature records,
-inspection reports.
Drivers must:
-protect all shipping documents,
-obtain signatures when required,
-verify document accuracy,
-submit PODs promptly after delivery.
Missing, damaged, altered, or late documentation may negatively impact company billing and 
customer relations.
Repeated document handling failures may result in operational penalties or disciplinary action.

sections.title: 6. TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED FREIGHT PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers operating temperature-controlled equipment are responsible for maintaining required 
temperature conditions.
Drivers must:
-verify temperature settings before departure,
-monitor reefer operation,
-confirm fuel levels,
-report reefer malfunctions immediately,
•maintain temperature records when required.
Drivers must immediately report:
-temperature deviations,
-reefer shutdowns,
-cargo contamination,
-frozen or spoiled freight,
-customer complaints involving temperature.
Failure to properly monitor refrigerated freight may result in cargo claims, operational penalties, or 
disciplinary action.

sections.title: 7. CARGO SECUREMENT PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for ensuring cargo is properly secured and transported safely.
Drivers must:
-inspect load securement,
-verify straps and locks,
-monitor load shifts,
-recheck securement during transit,
-comply with FMCSA cargo securement regulations.
Drivers must immediately report:
-shifted loads,
-damaged securement equipment,
-overloaded conditions,
-unsafe loading practices.
Unsafe cargo securement may result in:
-roadside violations,
-cargo claims,
-accidents,
-operational penalties,
-suspension.

sections.title: 8. CARGO DAMAGE & SHORTAGE REPORTING
sections.body:
Drivers must immediately report:
-damaged freight,
-shortages,
-overages,
-contamination,
-shifted loads,
-rejected freight,
-broken packaging,
-missing items.
Drivers must:
-take clear photos,
-protect freight from additional damage,
-maintain shipping documents,
-follow dispatch instructions.
Failure to properly report cargo incidents may increase cargo claim exposure and negatively 
impact company operations.
Negligence involving freight protection or failure to report incidents may result in operational 
penalties or chargebacks.

sections.title: 9. LUMPER & ACCESSORIAL REPORTING
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for properly reporting:
-lumper fees,
-detention,
-layover,
-TONU,
-extra stops,
-accessorial charges.
Drivers must submit:
-receipts,
-signed documents,
-supporting paperwork,
-required photos when requested.
Late or missing documentation may result in denied reimbursement or operational review.
Drivers must immediately notify dispatch regarding unexpected charges or delivery issues.

sections.title: 10. FREIGHT CLAIM LIABILITY & CHARGEBACKS
sections.body:
Moontera LLC reserves the right to review cargo claims, freight incidents, customer complaints, 
and operational losses involving preventable negligence.
Operational penalties, cargo claim reviews, chargebacks, or disciplinary action may result from:
-preventable freight damage,
-seal violations,
-improper securement,
-temperature negligence,
-unauthorized delays,
-missing documents,
-unreported shortages,
-customer complaints,
-rejected freight caused by driver negligence.
Examples of operational reviews may include:
-cargo claim investigations,
-freight damage costs,
-lumper disputes,
-detention losses,
-insurance-related expenses,
-customer service failures.
Any operational penalties, deductions, or chargebacks will be supported by documentation and 
handled in accordance with applicable laws and contractual agreements.
The company reserves the right to determine appropriate corrective action based on:
-severity,
-frequency,
-customer impact,
-operational damages,
-safety concerns.

sections.title: 11. FINAL DRIVER ACKNOWLEDGMENT
sections.body:
I acknowledge that I have received, reviewed, and understood the Moontera LLC Cargo Claims & 
Freight Handling Policy.
I understand that I am responsible for protecting customer freight, following cargo handling 
procedures, maintaining proper documentation, and immediately reporting freight-related incidents 
while operating under company authority.
I understand that violations of cargo handling procedures may result in disciplinary action, 
operational penalties, cargo claim reviews, chargebacks, suspension, removal from dispatch, 
contract termination, or termination of employment.

sections.title: Company notice
sections.body:
This document contains required emergency procedures, accident reporting requirements, 
operational safety procedures, maintenance reporting expectations, and incident response 
policies applicable to all drivers operating under Moontera LLC authority. Drivers are required to 
immediately report accidents, cargo incidents, roadside inspections, breakdowns, unsafe 
operating conditions, and equipment damages. Failure to follow company emergency procedures 
may negatively impact safety compliance, insurance protection, customer relationships, cargo 
claims, and company operations. Failure to comply with the procedures contained in this 
document may result in disciplinary action, operational penalties, suspension, removal from 
dispatch, contract termination, or termination of employment.

sections.title: 1. EMERGENCY CONTACT PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers must immediately contact dispatch or company management during any emergency 
situation involving:
-accidents,
-injuries,
-breakdowns,
-cargo damage,
-cargo theft,
-roadside inspections,
-law enforcement contact,
-unsafe weather conditions,
-hazardous road conditions,
-equipment failures.
Drivers must provide:
-exact location,
-truck and trailer number,
-load number,
-description of emergency,
-police or emergency response information,
-photos when available.
Drivers may not abandon company equipment or customer freight without company authorization.

sections.title: 2. ACCIDENT REPORTING PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Any accident involving company equipment, customer freight, personal injury, property damage, or 
law enforcement must be reported immediately.
Drivers involved in an accident must:
1.Stop immediately.
2.Secure the scene safely.
3.Call 911 if injuries or hazards exist.
4.Notify dispatch immediately.
5.Cooperate with law enforcement.
6.Obtain:
opolice report information,
owitness information,
oinsurance information,
ophotos of vehicles, cargo, and roadway.
Drivers may NOT:
-admit fault,
-argue at the scene,
-discuss insurance coverage,
-leave the scene without authorization.
Failure to immediately report accidents may result in:
-suspension,
-removal from dispatch,
-operational penalties,
-or termination.

sections.title: 3. PREVENTABLE ACCIDENT POLICY
sections.body:
Moontera LLC maintains strict accident prevention standards.
A preventable accident may include:
-backing accidents,
-striking fixed objects,
-rollover accidents,
-avoidable collisions,
-cargo securement failures,
-unsafe speed for conditions,
-distracted driving incidents,
-weather-related negligence.
Drivers are expected to operate defensively and safely at all times.
The company reserves the right to review all accidents and determine preventability.
Preventable accidents may result in:
-safety retraining,
-suspension,
-operational penalties,
-insurance-related restrictions,
-or termination.
Severe negligence, reckless driving, or repeated accidents may result in immediate termination.

sections.title: 4. BREAKDOWN & ROADSIDE EMERGENCY PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers must immediately report:
-mechanical failures,
-tire blowouts,
-engine warnings,
-air leaks,
-lighting failures,
-overheating,
-unsafe operating conditions.
Drivers must provide:
-exact location,
-fault codes,
-description of issue,
-whether vehicle is movable,
-photos when requested.
Drivers must:
-activate hazard lights,
-place warning triangles when required,
-remain with equipment unless authorized,
-protect customer freight.
Unauthorized repairs are prohibited unless approved by company management.
Failure to properly report breakdowns or protect equipment may result in operational penalties or 
disciplinary action.

sections.title: 5. WINTER WEATHER & UNSAFE DRIVING CONDITIONS POLICY
sections.body:
Safety takes priority over delivery schedules.
Drivers must reduce speed and operate cautiously during:
-snow,
-ice,
-fog,
-heavy rain,
-strong winds,
-low visibility,
-hazardous road conditions.
Drivers are authorized to stop operations when conditions become unsafe.
Drivers must immediately notify dispatch when:
-shutting down due to weather,
-delays are expected,
-roads become unsafe,
-chain laws are active.
Unsafe operation during severe weather may result in disciplinary action.
Drivers are expected to use professional judgment and operate safely at all times.

sections.title: 6. ROADSIDE INSPECTION PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers must immediately notify dispatch after any roadside inspection.
Drivers must:
-remain professional,
-cooperate with enforcement officers,
-provide required documents,
-submit inspection reports promptly.
Drivers must immediately report:
-violations,
-out-of-service orders,
-citations,
-equipment defects.
Failure to report roadside inspections or violations may result in disciplinary action.
DOT violations caused by negligence or failure to properly inspect equipment may result in 
operational penalties or retraining.

sections.title: 7. VEHICLE DAMAGE REPORTING PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers must immediately report:
-body damage,
-trailer damage,
-windshield damage,
-tire damage,
-interior damage,
-cargo securement damage,
-collision-related damage.
Failure to report damages may increase repair expenses and negatively impact operations.
Drivers may be subject to operational penalties, retraining, or disciplinary action for preventable 
damages caused by negligence or unsafe operation.

sections.title: 8. MAINTENANCE REPORTING PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers are responsible for monitoring the safe operating condition of company equipment.
Drivers must immediately report:
-engine warnings,
-fluid leaks,
-brake issues,
-tire issues,
-suspension problems,
-lighting problems,
-trailer defects.
Failure to report known defects may result in:
-additional equipment damages,
-DOT violations,
-safety risks,
-operational penalties.
Drivers may not continue operating unsafe equipment without authorization.

sections.title: 9. CARGO DAMAGE & FREIGHT INCIDENT PROCEDURE
sections.body:
Drivers must immediately report:
-damaged freight,
-shifted loads,
-rejected freight,
-broken seals,
-shortages,
-overages,
-temperature issues,
-cargo contamination.
Drivers must:
-take photos,
-secure the freight,
-follow dispatch instructions,
-protect shipping documents.
Drivers may not dispose of, transfer, or alter freight without company authorization.
Failure to properly report or protect cargo may result in:
-cargo claims,
-operational penalties,
-customer complaints,
-disciplinary action.

sections.title: 10. POST-ACCIDENT DRUG & ALCOHOL TESTING
sections.body:
Drivers may be required to complete post-accident drug and alcohol testing in accordance with 
FMCSA regulations and company policy.
Failure to cooperate with required testing procedures may result in:
-immediate removal from duty,
-suspension,
-termination,
-FMCSA reporting.
Drivers may not consume alcohol or prohibited substances following an accident until testing 
requirements are completed or officially waived.

sections.title: 11. FINAL DRIVER ACKNOWLEDGMENT
sections.body:
I acknowledge that I have received, reviewed, and understood the Moontera LLC Accident & 
Emergency Procedures Policy. I understand that I am responsible for following all emergency 
procedures, safety requirements, reporting expectations, and operational instructions while 
operating under company authority. I understand that failure to comply with company emergency 
procedures may result in disciplinary action, operational penalties, suspension, removal from 
dispatch, contract termination, or termination of employment.
